learning_outcomes.text: Students learn to calculate the acting forces at the support and connection points, at smooth and frictional contact points of the systems, and within the structural elements themselves for technical structural systems designed as two- and three-dimensional multi-part rigid body systems.

syllabus_topics: Decomposition of technical structural systems into individual components or suitable substructures
Identification of interacting forces between elements through free-body diagrams
Formulation of systems of friction and equilibrium conditions
Solving systems of equations for magnitudes and directions of forces
Use of acquired knowledge for determining mechanical stresses of machine elements and components
Use of acquired knowledge for selecting, designing, and dimensioning elements based on load
Use of acquired knowledge for verifying strength or service life
assessment_rules: The graded assessment is a 120-minute written exam. A prerequisite for the exam is successfully passing several homework assignments distributed throughout the semester with at least 75% of the total achievable score. The examination immediately after the first semester is compulsory.
bibliography: Gross, D.; Hauger, W.; Schröder, J., Wall, W. A.: Technische Mechanik 1 – Statik. Springer 2006
